content:
You are writing the BODY of a cover letter for this candidate. You are not given the job description for this application, so write from the candidate's own experience and what the role and company imply - and the candidate's profile below is the only source of fact (when a resume was tailored for this application, the profile carries that resume's summary and bullets, which are then the experience to write from): every employer, project, figure, technology, customer, colleague and outcome you mention is in it, or it is not in the letter.

PROFILE:
[[profileJson]]

APPLICATION:
Company: [[companyName]]
Role: [[role]]

3-4 paragraphs. No salutation, no sign-off, no bullet points.

The first word is "I", and the whole letter is first person. Never open a sentence with a resume-style action verb ("Designed...", "Executed..."). Vary sentence length; mix short and long.

Open with genuine enthusiasm for this kind of work, with the span of years and the domain the profile states - and no span at all when it states none. Tell one specific achievement FROM THE PROFILE as a brief story connecting to this role, with only the details the profile gives it. Add a second moment, also from the profile, showing personality and real technical depth: a problem a bullet describes, a tool a role lists, a decision the summary records. Say what actually excites you about this work and this company, drawn from what the profile shows the candidate has chosen to do. Close confidently, in a line that does not sound templated. No clichés, and nothing like "I look forward to hearing from you".

Where the profile gives little, the letter is shorter and plainer, never fuller. Do not round a figure, re-base it, or state one the profile does not state. Do not name a product, a customer, a team size, a colleague or a technology the profile does not name. Do not claim a skill or a domain the role implies and the profile lacks: write about the adjacent thing the candidate has actually done.

It has to be warm, specific to this candidate, and compelling enough to earn an interview.

Write plainly, the way an engineer talks about their own work. NEVER use these words in any form: leveraged, utilized, spearheaded, orchestrated, streamlined, seamless, robust, scalable, maximized, cross-functional, end-to-end, innovative, dynamic, cutting-edge, world-class, state-of-the-art, holistic, comprehensive, proven, strategic. Do not open sentences with Designed, Architected, Led, Delivered, Drove, Integrated, Partnered, Supported, Contributed, Managed or Streamlined - use built, wrote, shipped, cut, rewrote, fixed, migrated, ran. No metaphors. Concise, not verbose. Never use em-dashes, and never write "--" or "–" in place of one: use a comma, a colon or a full stop. Never invent an achievement, employer or metric, and never a technology or anecdote, that is not in the profile.

Return only the cover letter body text. No JSON, no markdown, no commentary.
